A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIFT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original GIFT fine-tuning experiments across language and vision tasks, ablations, and qualitative generation and localization results.

after.justification: v4 retains original language and vision experiments and reports revised GIFT reasoning results and newly trained VeRA comparisons.

M1.justification: The two-linear-layer weight-residual generator remains. v4 adds output-dimension adaptation for Output and Down projections and a block-wise variant with separate generators per Transformer block and sharing within QKV and Up/Gate groups (Sections 1.2 and 3). These extend the application and sharing procedure beyond v3's variants.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca52k, Ultrafeedback and Alpaca-Eval, the same eight commonsense and four arithmetic benchmarks, six GLUE tasks, five FGVC datasets, and VTAB-1k. Relocated GLUE and VTAB results remain present in v4's appendix.

E2.justification: VeRA is added to the commonsense and arithmetic comparisons in Tables 2–3; v3 evaluated it only on GLUE. The other comparator sets are retained. Although v4's arithmetic discussion mentions DoRA, Table 3 contains no DoRA result, so this is not an added evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Reasoning training changes from six commonsense or twelve arithmetic epochs to three, and from batch size eight with four accumulation steps to sixteen with one. Search grids change, and commonsense hyperparameter tuning moves from GSM8k to BoolQ (v3 Appendix A.2; v4 B.3–B.4). v4 also specifies zero-phi initialization for vision and GLUE, revising v3's general zero-psi prescription; this does not establish reruns of their unchanged results.

E4.justification: The reasoning comparisons revise the investigation of where to apply GIFT, introducing evidence about Output/Down adaptation and within-block sharing (Tables 2–3). The nonlinear-generator and vision-layer ablations remain unchanged, as do the visual localization examples; several are relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report two instruction-following runs, three reasoning runs, and the same corresponding seeds. GLUE retains its five-seed median protocol, ± reporting, and unstable-seed replacement disclosure. No new confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace GIFT reasoning results under revised settings: rank-64 QKVUD reports Llama-3 commonsense accuracy of 86.5 instead of 82.5 and LLaMA-1 arithmetic accuracy of 49.2 instead of 46.8. The new block-wise variant reports 87.7 and 49.8, respectively. VeRA scores and runtime/memory comparisons are added, and the LLaMA-1 OBQA example changes from answer4 to answer3. Instruction-following, GLUE, and vision scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 revises the output-dimension formulation and gradient example, using a three-layer MLP with selected layers fine-tuned. It also changes the activation-space derivation: v3 Equation 11 correctly uses psi-transpose times phi-transpose, whereas v4 Equation 9 uses phi times psi despite retaining the same weight-update definition. The displayed equality is therefore inconsistent.

C1.justification: The headline contributions shift from built-in interpretability to bridging PEFT and ReFT and maintaining memory efficiency. Visual interpretability disappears from the abstract and conclusion, although its evidence remains. The abstract/conclusion also strengthen arithmetic-reasoning performance from comparable performance to outperforming baselines.

C2.justification: v3's explicit limitations concerning unexplained cluster emergence, manual inspection, inconsistent clusters across instances, and uncertain applicability to language models are removed. v4 adds interpretations that block-wise sharing is robust across tasks and that VeRA's training cost makes it prohibitive for large benchmarks, replacing parts of the earlier task-dependent layer-selection discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds residual scaling by alpha/r, Kaiming initialization, explicit decoding and token limits, and expanded method-specific reasoning settings. v4 identifies the HuggingFace VeRA implementation and reports language-training time and memory. Direct GIFT and PyReFT repository links disappear, while the project-page link remains and supplementary code is mentioned. Newly disclosed scaling and decoding details do not themselves establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially expand positioning against DoRA, VeRA, LoReFT, and DiReFT, explicitly describing GIFT as sharing-oriented LoRA and a PEFT–ReFT bridge. Citations to Geiger et al., He et al., and Taori et al. are added. The hypernetwork and neural-functional positioning is largely retained; bibliographic updates alone are not substantive changes.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, approach narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The introduction gains motivation and method-overview subsections, background is reorganized, and GLUE, VTAB results, and the vision-layer ablation move into an expanded appendix structure.

P2.justification: v4 redesigns and combines v3's method schematic and performance plots into Figure 1, adding an arithmetic panel. Reasoning tables are regrouped, Table 1 becomes a narrow display beside text, and several tables and localization figures move. Captions, headers, and generation-example boxes are also restyled.

improvement.justification: v4 improves comparative evidence through VeRA evaluations, sharing variants, and resource measurements, and supplies useful reproducibility details. However, it introduces an algebraic inconsistency into the prominently claimed PEFT–ReFT bridge (Equation 9) and removes specific interpretability limitations while retaining localization claims. These competing gains in empirical documentation and losses in mathematical reliability and qualification prevent a confident net quality judgment.
